## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}

```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false

```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
# Establishing the subset
trad_data <- acs2021_couples %>%
  filter(SEX == "Female", h_sex == 1, RELATE == 2, AGE >= 18, h_age >= 18)

#Establishing the dependent dummy variable

trad_data$age_diff <- trad_data$AGE - trad_data$h_age

trad_data$he_more_than_5yrs_than_her <- as.numeric(trad_data$age_diff < -5)
```

```{r}
table(trad_data$he_more_than_5yrs_than_her,cut(trad_data$age_diff,c(-100,-10, -5, 0, 5, 10, 100)))
mean(trad_data$he_more_than_5yrs_than_her)
```

```{r}
# Establishing dummies for independent variable of REGION. Since the couple lives in the same household, it will be the same variable for both spouses, so only one set of dummies.

trad_data$REGION_f <- factor(trad_data$REGION,
                             levels = c(11, 12, 21, 22, 31, 32, 33, 41, 42),
                             labels = c("New England", "Middle Atlantic", "East North Central",
                                        "West North Central", "South Atlantic", "East South Central",
                                        "West South Central", "Mountain", "Pacific"))
trad_data$REGION_f <- relevel(trad_data$REGION_f, ref = "South Atlantic")

#Establishing dummies for independent variable of Race. For the wife (RACE) and husband (h_race), base = White.
race_labels <- c("White", "Black", "American Indian or Alaska Native",
                 "Chinese", "Japanese", "Other Asian or Pacific Islander",
                 "Other race", "Two races", "Three or more races")

trad_data$wife_race <- factor(as.numeric(as.character(trad_data$RACE)),
                              levels = 1:9, labels = race_labels)
trad_data$hus_race  <- factor(as.numeric(as.character(trad_data$h_race)),
                              levels = 1:9, labels = race_labels)

class(trad_data$wife_race)  

# Establishing dummies for independent variable  of Education Levels. For the wife (EDUC) and husband (h_educ), 5 categories. Base = less than high school. (3 yrs college has 0 obs in this file.)
educ_cat <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  case_when(
    x == "Grade 12"                                              ~ "HS",
    x %in% c("1 year of college", "2 years of college",
             "3 years of college")                               ~ "Some college",
    x == "4 years of college"                                    ~ "College",
    x == "5+ years of college"                                   ~ "Advanced degree",
    TRUE                                                         ~ "Less than HS"
  )
}
lv <- c("Less than HS", "HS", "Some college", "College", "Advanced degree")
trad_data$wife_educ <- factor(educ_cat(trad_data$EDUC),   levels = lv)
trad_data$hus_educ  <- factor(educ_cat(trad_data$h_educ), levels = lv)

trad_data <- trad_data %>% mutate(
  wife_hs       = as.numeric(wife_educ == "HS"),
  wife_somecoll = as.numeric(wife_educ == "Some college"),
  wife_college  = as.numeric(wife_educ == "College"),
  wife_advdeg   = as.numeric(wife_educ == "Advanced degree"),
  hus_hs        = as.numeric(hus_educ  == "HS"),
  hus_somecoll  = as.numeric(hus_educ  == "Some college"),
  hus_college   = as.numeric(hus_educ  == "College"),
  hus_advdeg    = as.numeric(hus_educ  == "Advanced degree")
)
```

```{r}
dat_use <- trad_data
```

```{r}
# Turning every x-factor into 0/1 dummies, in one step:

X_mat <- model.matrix(~ REGION_f + wife_race + hus_race + wife_educ + hus_educ,data = dat_use)[, -1]
```

```{r}
# Cleaning up the column names so they work in formulas and read nicely
colnames(X_mat) <- make.names(colnames(X_mat))
colnames(X_mat) <- sub("^REGION_f", "Reg_", colnames(X_mat))
colnames(X_mat) <- sub("^wife_race", "W_race_", colnames(X_mat))
colnames(X_mat) <- sub("^hus_race",  "H_race_", colnames(X_mat))
colnames(X_mat) <- sub("^wife_educ", "W_educ_", colnames(X_mat))
colnames(X_mat) <- sub("^hus_educ",  "H_educ_", colnames(X_mat))

colnames(X_mat)
```

```{r}
# Putting Y and X dummies together
dat_for_analysis_sub <- data.frame(
  he_more_than_5yrs_than_her = dat_use$he_more_than_5yrs_than_her,
  X_mat)
```

```{r}
# Checking for empty dummies: it prints to zero :D
sum(colSums(X_mat) == 0)
```

```{r}
# Training and Test Split
set.seed(654321)
NN <- nrow(dat_for_analysis_sub)

train_frac <- 0.10
restrict_1 <- (runif(NN) < train_frac)
summary(restrict_1)

dat_train <- subset(dat_for_analysis_sub,  restrict_1)
dat_test  <- subset(dat_for_analysis_sub, !restrict_1)

# Checking again: it's zero :D
sum(colSums(dat_train) == 0)
```

```{r}
# Checking the outcome shares are similar in train and test:
mean(dat_train$he_more_than_5yrs_than_her)
mean(dat_test$he_more_than_5yrs_than_her)

# They're approximately similar: 1) ~0.189; 2) ~0.187
```

```{r}
# Standardizing using training data 
formula_sobj <- reformulate(names(dat_for_analysis_sub)[-1],
                            response = "he_more_than_5yrs_than_her")

sobj <- standardize(formula_sobj, dat_train, family = binomial)

s_dat_test <- predict(sobj, dat_test)
```

```{r}
# OLS (linear probability model): fit on training, evaluate on test:
model_lpm1 <- lm(sobj$formula, data = sobj$data)
summary(model_lpm1)

pred_vals_lpm   <- predict(model_lpm1, s_dat_test)
pred_model_lpm1 <- (pred_vals_lpm > mean(pred_vals_lpm))
table(pred = pred_model_lpm1, true = dat_test$he_more_than_5yrs_than_her)
```

```{r}
# Logit: fit on training, evaluate on test:
model_logit1 <- glm(sobj$formula, family = binomial, data = sobj$data)
summary(model_logit1)

pred_vals_logit   <- predict(model_logit1, s_dat_test, type = "response")
pred_model_logit1 <- (pred_vals_logit > mean(pred_vals_logit))
table(pred = pred_model_logit1, true = dat_test$he_more_than_5yrs_than_her)
```

```{r}
# Lab 9 Part 1 - Splitting the Data
trad_data$BA_plus <- trad_data$wife_college + trad_data$wife_advdeg
table(trad_data$BA_plus)
```

```{r}
# Whole dataset, full interaction)
model_lpm_v1 <- lm(he_more_than_5yrs_than_her ~ BA_plus + AGE + I(AGE * BA_plus), data = trad_data)
summary(model_lpm_v1)
```

```{r}
# Two subsets, rather than the whole dataset:
dat_use_BAplus <- trad_data %>% filter(as.logical(BA_plus))
dat_use_ltBA   <- trad_data %>% filter(!as.logical(BA_plus))

model_lpm_v1_BAplus <- lm(he_more_than_5yrs_than_her ~ AGE, data = dat_use_BAplus)
model_lpm_v1_ltBA   <- lm(he_more_than_5yrs_than_her ~ AGE, data = dat_use_ltBA)
summary(model_lpm_v1_BAplus)
summary(model_lpm_v1_ltBA)
```

```{r}
# Seeing that the two approaches are identical
b <- coef(model_lpm_v1)
rbind(full_model = c(ltBA_int   = unname(b["(Intercept)"]),
               ltBA_slope = unname(b["AGE"]),
               BA_int     = unname(b["(Intercept)"] + b["BA_plus"]),
               BA_slope   = unname(b["AGE"] + b["I(AGE * BA_plus)"])),
split_models = c(coef(model_lpm_v1_ltBA), coef(model_lpm_v1_BAplus))
```

```{r}
# Predictions for every person are identical
pred_full  <- predict(model_lpm_v1, trad_data)
pred_split <- ifelse(trad_data$BA_plus == 1,
                     predict(model_lpm_v1_BAplus, trad_data),
                     predict(model_lpm_v1_ltBA,   trad_data))
all.equal(unname(pred_full), unname(pred_split))
```

```{r}
# The Setup to be Shared by All the Machine-Learning Models
y_name  <- "he_more_than_5yrs_than_her"
x_names <- setdiff(names(sobj$data), y_name)
stopifnot(all(x_names %in% names(s_dat_test)))

X_train <- data.matrix(sobj$data[, x_names])
y_train <- sobj$data[[y_name]]
X_test  <- data.matrix(s_dat_test[, x_names])
y_test  <- dat_test[[y_name]]
base_rate <- mean(y_test)

to_lgl <- function(p) if (is.logical(p)) p else as.numeric(as.character(p)) == 1

eval_model <- function(flag, truth, name) {
  flag <- to_lgl(flag)
  tp <- sum(flag & truth == 1);  fp <- sum(flag & truth == 0)
  fn <- sum(!flag & truth == 1); tn <- sum(!flag & truth == 0)
  data.frame(model = name,
             accuracy  = (tp + tn) / length(truth),
             recall    = tp / (tp + fn),
             precision = ifelse(tp + fp > 0, tp / (tp + fp), NA),
             flagged = tp + fp, TP = tp, FP = fp, FN = fn, TN = tn)
}
cut_mean <- function(score) score > mean(score)   # same mean cutoff as before

results <- rbind(
  eval_model(cut_mean(pred_vals_lpm),   y_test, "OLS (mean cutoff)"),
  eval_model(cut_mean(pred_vals_logit), y_test, "Logit (mean cutoff)")
)
```

```{r}
# PART 3. Random forest
set.seed(54321)
model_randFor <- randomForest(as.factor(he_more_than_5yrs_than_her) ~ .,
                              data = sobj$data, importance = TRUE,
                              ntree = 200)
print(model_randFor)               # confusion matrix here is within the training data (OOB)
round(importance(model_randFor), 2)
varImpPlot(model_randFor)

# (a) The lab's default: majority-vote class prediction on the TEST data
pred_rf_class <- predict(model_randFor, s_dat_test)
table(pred = pred_rf_class, true = y_test)

# (b) Same mean-cutoff rule as the OLS and logit, using predicted probabilities
rf_prob <- predict(model_randFor, s_dat_test, type = "prob")[, "1"]
results <- rbind(results,
                 eval_model(pred_rf_class,      y_test, "Random forest (majority vote)"),
                 eval_model(cut_mean(rf_prob),  y_test, "Random forest (mean cutoff)"))
```

```{r}
# PART 4. Support vector machine
set.seed(54321)
svm_n      <- 10000
svm_test_n <- 50000
svm_idx    <- sample(nrow(sobj$data), min(svm_n, nrow(sobj$data)))
svm_t_idx  <- sample(nrow(s_dat_test), min(svm_test_n, nrow(s_dat_test)))

svm.model <- svm(as.factor(he_more_than_5yrs_than_her) ~ .,
                 data = sobj$data[svm_idx, ], cost = 1, gamma = 0.1)

# (a) default class prediction
svm.pred <- predict(svm.model, s_dat_test[svm_t_idx, ])
table(pred = svm.pred, true = y_test[svm_t_idx])

# (b) mean cutoff on the decision value.
svm_dec <- as.numeric(attr(predict(svm.model, s_dat_test[svm_t_idx, ],
                                   decision.values = TRUE), "decision.values"))
if (cor(svm_dec, pred_vals_logit[svm_t_idx]) < 0) svm_dec <- -svm_dec
results <- rbind(results,
                 eval_model(svm.pred,          y_test[svm_t_idx], "SVM (class, 50k test sample)"),
                 eval_model(cut_mean(svm_dec), y_test[svm_t_idx], "SVM (mean cutoff, 50k test sample)"))
```

```{r}
# PART 5. Elastic net (LASSO + ridge)
model1_elasticnet <- glmnet(X_train, y_train)         
print(model1_elasticnet)
plot(model1_elasticnet, label = TRUE)

set.seed(54321)
foldid <- sample(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(X_train))) 
cvmodel1_elasticnet <- cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, foldid = foldid)
cvmodel1_elasticnet$lambda.min
log(cvmodel1_elasticnet$lambda.min)
coef(cvmodel1_elasticnet, s = "lambda.min")  

pred1_elasnet <- as.numeric(predict(cvmodel1_elasticnet, newx = X_test, s = "lambda.min"))
results <- rbind(results,
                 eval_model(cut_mean(pred1_elasnet), y_test, "LASSO (alpha=1, mean cutoff)"))

# Trying other alphas (0 = ridge, 1 = LASSO) and keep the one with the lowest CV error
alphas  <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)
cv_list <- lapply(alphas, function(a) cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, alpha = a, foldid = foldid))
data.frame(alpha = alphas, cv_error = sapply(cv_list, function(m) min(m$cvm)))
best <- which.min(sapply(cv_list, function(m) min(m$cvm)))
pred_en_best <- as.numeric(predict(cv_list[[best]], newx = X_test, s = "lambda.min"))
results <- rbind(results,
                 eval_model(cut_mean(pred_en_best), y_test,
                            paste0("Elastic net (alpha=", alphas[best], ", mean cutoff)")))

# Optional: logistic elastic net (family = binomial) for a probability-based version
cv_en_logit <- cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, family = "binomial", alpha = 1, foldid = foldid)
pred_en_logit <- as.numeric(predict(cv_en_logit, newx = X_test, s = "lambda.min", type = "response"))
results <- rbind(results,
                 eval_model(cut_mean(pred_en_logit), y_test, "LASSO logit (mean cutoff)"))
```

```{r}
# PART 6. Spike and slab
set.seed(54321)
model1_spikeslab <- spikeslab(sobj$formula, data = sobj$data)
print(model1_spikeslab)
summary(model1_spikeslab)
plot(model1_spikeslab)

ss_pred  <- predict(model1_spikeslab, newdata = s_dat_test)
ss_score <- as.numeric(ss_pred$yhat.gnet)    
results <- rbind(results,
                 eval_model(cut_mean(ss_score), y_test, "Spike and slab (mean cutoff)"))
```

```{r}
# PART 7. Comparing all the models
results_print <- results
results_print[, c("accuracy", "recall", "precision")] <-
  round(results_print[, c("accuracy", "recall", "precision")], 3)
results_print
base_rate                 

# --- Do the models make the same errors? ---
scores <- data.frame(OLS = pred_vals_lpm, Logit = pred_vals_logit,
                     LASSO = pred1_elasnet, RF = rf_prob)
round(cor(scores), 2)     # near 1 = models rank couples almost identically

table(Logit = cut_mean(pred_vals_logit), RF = cut_mean(rf_prob))   # where they disagree

# --- Simple ensemble: average the probabilities, then use the mean cutoff ---
ens <- rowMeans(scores)
results <- rbind(results,
                 eval_model(cut_mean(ens), y_test, "Ensemble (OLS+Logit+LASSO+RF)"))
tail(results, 1)

# --- Which X variables matter consistently? ---
zt <- summary(model_logit1)$coefficients
rownames(zt) <- sub("1$", "", rownames(zt))   # "Reg_New.England1" -> "Reg_New.England"
logit_z <- abs(zt[x_names, "z value"])

lasso_c <- as.numeric(coef(cvmodel1_elasticnet, s = "lambda.min")[x_names, ])
rf_gini <- importance(model_randFor)[x_names, "MeanDecreaseGini"]
var_tab <- data.frame(variable = x_names,
                      logit_abs_z = round(logit_z, 2),
                      lasso_coef  = round(lasso_c, 4),
                      lasso_kept  = lasso_c != 0,
                      rf_gini     = round(rf_gini, 1),
                      rank_logit  = rank(-logit_z),
                      rank_rf     = rank(-rf_gini))
var_tab[order(var_tab$rank_logit + var_tab$rank_rf), ]

# --- Subgroups: accuracy for BA+ wives vs. others ---
ba_test <- dat_test$W_educ_College == 1 | dat_test$W_educ_Advanced.degree == 1
rbind(
  BA_plus  = eval_model(cut_mean(pred_vals_logit)[ba_test],  y_test[ba_test],  "Logit, wife BA+"),
  below_BA = eval_model(cut_mean(pred_vals_logit)[!ba_test], y_test[!ba_test], "Logit, wife < BA")
)
```
